hypotheses.summary: Both DRAM and NAND tightened, but DRAM oligopoly/content growth and NAND 3D-transition friction may explain different supply mechanics.
Both lines weakened after the boom while NAND had additional Yokkaichi/JV-specific disturbances; timing and severity should be verified separately.
Pandemic PC/cloud/mobile mix affected both lines, while DDR5, HBM and enterprise SSD qualification introduced product-specific lags.
Both lines entered a severe inventory correction, but supplier cut timing and NAND supply structure may have produced different price/recovery paths.

HBM and some server DRAM may have diverged positively from conventional DRAM while enterprise SSD/QLC created a distinct NAND demand lane; ordinary supply cuts/inventory normalization remain alternative explanations for broad recovery.
Shared-company capex and management allocation can couple DRAM and NAND cycles even when fabs, bit growth, price and qualification metrics are not interchangeable.

hard_guard: No hypothesis is Reality; Stage B must seek dated claim-scoped evidence and preserve divergence instead of forcing one memory cycle.
